name: Carlkin
slug: Carlkin is a turtle-like person believed to be back in Langdale.
description: Carlkin is a turtle-like person associated with Langdale.

log.summary: The party considered asking Carlkin for information about The Reach or Grixto. Sylan recalled Carlkin as the turtle-like person and believed he was currently back in Langdale.
notes: The party considers asking Carlkin for information about The Reach or Grixto.
Sylan recalls Carlkin as the turtle-like person and believes he is currently back in Langdale.

log.summary: Sylan, Gerk, Dana, and Ord visit Carlkin at his lighthouse in New Navel during the two days before Walker is expected back, hoping he has a lead; he is not away in Langdale. His door carries mixed-script notices (no loitering, appointments only), which he says he wrote in sixteen languages. He rejects Gerk’s reading of “Knock loud. Be let in,” shouts after the third blow, claims he knows no “girls,” and refuses them without an appointment. Gerk throws the door open into crates and books while Carlkin is holding it. He says he is busy studying, fails to shove Gerk back out, and demands Sylan get to the point. Dana calls him one of the original holders; Ord calls him a useful resource they need not distrust. Sylan is unsure they have spoken before and had forgotten his voice. They agree not to hide their relics. The ground floor is cluttered with crates, maps, tomes (including a first edition of the Sea of Nyx), and a snoring pile of books. When the doorway opens onto the abyss he dives behind the books, furious that Gerk tested the power in the shop. A tentacle scatters his books; he throws one at the metal sleeper, calls it a tin can, and yells for it to wake because hooligans summoned the beast. Treated as an ally, he takes Ord’s initiative bonus, rolls 25, and acts after Gerk on lower Dexterity. Warned out of the splash zone, he runs for the stairs. Already running when the wall of eyes appears, he makes no Wisdom save, and his footsteps fade upstairs.
notes: Sylan hopes he has a lead. During the two days before Walker is expected back, Sylan, Gerk, Dana, and Ord visit him. He is at his lighthouse in New Navel, which the party has entered once or twice, and is present for the fight. He is not away in Langdale.

His weathered wooden door carries mixed-script notices, including no loitering and appointments only. He says he wrote them in sixteen languages and expects visitors to read at least one. He rejects Gerk's reading of "Knock loud. Be let in." After the third blow he shouts to stop breaking the door, says he does not know any "girls," and refuses them for lack of an appointment. He is holding the door when Gerk throws it open into crates and books.

He calls himself very busy with studying and other appointments and tries and fails to shove Gerk back out. Dana says he was one of the original holders. Ord says he has been a useful resource and that the party has no reason to distrust him. Sylan is not sure they have actually talked before and had forgotten his voice. They agree not to hide their relics. He demands Sylan get to the point.

The ground floor is cluttered with crates, barrels, maps, tomes, porridge bowls, and papers, including a first edition of the Sea of Nyx that the party was part of, later additions, and very old tomes. A pile of books in the corner is snoring. The door swings shut behind the party almost by itself. A spiral staircase is on the far wall.

When the doorway opens onto the abyss he screams, dives behind the books, and is furious that Gerk tested the power in the shop. A tentacle scatters his books. He throws a book at the metal sleeper in the corner, calls it a tin can, and yells for it to wake because hooligans summoned the beast.

He is treated as an ally. He receives Ord's initiative bonus, rolls 25, and acts after Gerk because of lower Dexterity. When Sylan warns him out of the splash zone, he runs for the stairs and is allowed up to half his movement. He is already running when the wall of eyes appears, so he does not make the Wisdom save. His footsteps fade as he goes upstairs.

log.summary: Carlkin fled upstairs and refused to come down, questioning the party from above while he drank. He banned portals in the lighthouse and wanted the rule written at once with his good imported pen, not for Gerk. He had not known they still held the keystones, thinking they only collected them for Juten Prime, and had not heard of the finished delivery, the prophecy, or their greater importance. He treats the doorway as close to a portal to hell and threatens to leave for good if Gerk opens another there. Gerk's tears are his first news that Gerk's mother is dead; the blonde girl with flowers he calls a hallucination. He states Doorman cautions, calls the lighthouse door a door to nowhere, and thinks an astral being nearly birthed in his living room. Plymouth did not teach the dangers, including that a boat is forbidden. He calls Gerk a footman, is silenced by Grixto holding the Book of Vecna, thinks the phylactery is carried loot, and fears for Walker and his dragon. He will not test a Doorman and keystone there. Dana and Sylan connect the Reach legend to the lich; a shop bangle shows the party's magic is masked.
notes: Fled upstairs during the fight and will not come down. He shouts from the stairs, then through a knot in the floorboards, while he interrogates the party and drinks.
Imposes a house rule of no portals in the lighthouse and wants it written at once on his parchment with his good pen. The pen is not for Gerk. The quill and ink are well used, high-end, and imported.

Did not know the party still held the keystones. He thought they were only collecting them for Juten Prime, and he had not heard that the delivery was finished, that a prophecy followed, or that the party had become more important.
Treats the doorway as close to a portal to hell. He is furious it was opened in his home and threatens to teleport away for good if Gerk opens another door there.
Reads Gerk's tears as the first news he has had that Gerk's mother is dead and that Gerk is an orphan. He treats the blonde girl with flowers as a hallucination.

States Doorman rules: do not open a door on something moving, because it stays fixed and warps space from the opener's new position; do not open a door to an unknown place. A door with no chosen destination opens between the arches. Proper use is to name one specific familiar door and see yourself opening it.

Identifies the lighthouse door as a door to nowhere. He thinks the creature was an astral being, not simply an abomination, and that it nearly used his living room as a birthing place. He does not know what would happen if a Doorman and a keystone were pulled through such a door, and treats that ignorance as a reason not to try it.
Says Plymouth was present when Gerk learned the ability and did not teach the dangers, including that a boat is a forbidden site.

Will repair the broken cobbles and floor with Mending. He asks what else the party came for, says he is usually free Tuesdays at nine thirty, and keeps trying to turn the briefing into an appointment.
Confirms that people other than Gerk can open doors, and he does not name them. He withholds the title Doorman and calls Gerk a footman, the apprentice rank.

Withholds the names of Mother's Prayer scholars and keeps part of that scholarship in reserve. He resents the assumption that the man in the tower knows nothing. He states that trees are certainly alive.

Knows the Emperor of Nyx and already knew the hobgoblin realm had fallen into civil war. He does not know the name Grixto, or that the emperor was a lich. He already knew the Reach legend of Elrus, Garixto the Betrayer, Galixtar, and the Twin Bloody Comet, and had not connected it to this lich until Dana and Sylan named them.

News that Grixto has the Book of Vecna leaves him unable to speak. He then pours liquor instead of tea. He is frightened by a lich who can still contact the party and by abyss-doors opened in his home.

Serves a thin steaming tea-like drink from a jug like one Ord carries, and laces his own cup from a bottle in his desk. He keeps formal china, doilies, and a real silver platter for a proper visit. Benji is with him and speaks when Carlkin is at a loss.

Explains fixed keyed gates, gatekeeper portals, ley lines, and chained gatehouses. He argues the phylactery is likely loot they are still carrying, and that a two-way reply from Grixto sounds like Sending rather than a full mental link.

A shop bangle carries a residual detect magic that flags magical items brought inside. It did not flag the party, so he concludes their magic is masked. He notes it would not flag Gerk's door, because that is not a magical item.
Says time is strange on the Reach arch. He connects the lich's dragon-killing and theft of Al Kurin to an immediate worry about where Walker and his dragon are.

log.summary: At the lighthouse, with Ord, Gerk, and Sylan still there and a second voice this stretch does not separate from his, Carlkin says he and the people he speaks for were once gatekeepers. Their work was protection—receive a keystone and hide it—not doorkeeping, and he finds it strange that keystones are being handed out again after they were collected. A lich speaking to the party telepathically unsettles him; he tells them to deal with it immediately, and he has heard a rumor that the dragon in the mountains is dead. He tells Gerk to stop fixing a hole, says he will mend the floor later, and thanks them for trying. He wants practice only in the woods or a large field, never underwater and not in the lighthouse or his house, and says only Gerk can shut those doors. An unshut door stays a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses. He tells Gerk to put down the door dropping Gerk's arm, says Gerk's mother will not come through though everyone else will, and invokes Gerk and Gerk's dead mother at least three times. He drinks through the talk and is quite drunk by the end, still reeling from an eldritch horror brought into his living room. He would rather they book an appointment than arrive unannounced, and agrees to send a runner and schedule a look at a helm when their comrade returns. His location is much farther than five hundred feet from the castle.
notes: Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are still with him in the lighthouse on the day they already briefed him. A second person is present; the DM invites questions to either, and this stretch does not separate that voice from his.
